title: Neech bhanga raj yoga: when a debilitated planet recovers | Ask Tota
description: Neech bhanga cancels a planet's debilitation. The classical rules, a worked example for each planet, why cancellation is common, and when it becomes a raj yoga.
og_title: Neech bhanga raj yoga, rule by rule
og_description: A debilitated planet is not the end of the story. The classical cancellation rules, worked examples, and why texts say a recovered planet can rise high.
h1: neech bhanga raj yoga is the comeback rule for a debilitated planet
dek: a debilitated planet sits in the sign where it is weakest. classical texts then list several ways that weakness gets cancelled, and say a cancelled debilitation can even produce a raj yoga. the rules are specific, they are checkable, and they apply more often than people expect.
card_title: neech bhanga raj yoga is the comeback rule for a debilitated planet
card_dek: the classical rules that cancel debilitation, a worked example, and why a recovered planet is said to rise higher than an ordinary one.
llms_desc: what neecha bhanga (cancellation of debilitation) is, the classical rules from Phaladeepika and Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, worked examples, the debilitation and exaltation sign of each planet, when cancellation becomes a raj yoga, and myths about debilitated planets.

faq.q: what is neech bhanga raj yoga?
faq.a: a combination where a debilitated planet's weakness is cancelled by specific conditions, and the planet is then said to give strong, often rising results. neecha means debilitated, bhanga means broken, and raj yoga means a royal combination.

faq.q: what are the rules for neech bhanga?
faq.a: the main ones: the lord of the debilitation sign in a kendra from the lagna or moon; the lord of the planet's exaltation sign in a kendra; the planet that is exalted in that sign in a kendra; the debilitated planet aspected by its sign lord; or an exchange between the planet and its sign lord.
sun in libra, moon in scorpio, mars in cancer, mercury in pisces, jupiter in capricorn, venus in virgo, saturn in aries. each is debilitated in the sign opposite its exaltation.

fairly. there are several cancellation rules and each can be met from the lagna or the moon, so a good share of debilitated planets meet at least one. strength of the cancelling planets still matters.

faq.q: is a debilitated planet always bad?
faq.a: no. debilitation means the planet has difficulty expressing its significations easily. with cancellation, or good house placement and dasha timing, it can deliver well. many readers describe it as a planet that must work harder and so learns more.

faq.q: does neech bhanga make a planet exalted?
faq.a: no. it cancels the weakness rather than turning it into exaltation. classical texts say a cancelled debilitation can give results comparable to a raj yoga, often after early struggle.

faq.q: what is neech bhanga for jupiter in capricorn?
faq.a: jupiter's debilitation is cancelled if saturn, lord of capricorn, or the moon, lord of jupiter's exaltation sign cancer, or mars, which is exalted in capricorn, sits in a kendra from the lagna or the moon.

faq.q: what is neech bhanga for sun in libra?
faq.a: venus, lord of libra, or mars, lord of aries where the sun exalts, or saturn, exalted in libra, in a kendra from the lagna or moon cancels it. venus aspecting the sun also counts in many texts.

faq.q: does navamsa matter for neech bhanga?
faq.a: many astrologers check it. a planet debilitated in the d1 but exalted in the d9 navamsa is commonly read as recovering strength, and some count that as a form of cancellation.

faq.q: when does neech bhanga raj yoga give results?
faq.a: traditionally in the dasha or antardasha of the debilitated planet, or of the planets forming the cancellation. a common description is results arriving after initial difficulty.

faq.q: can a debilitated planet be retrograde?
faq.a: yes, mars, mercury, jupiter, venus and saturn can be. some traditions treat a retrograde debilitated planet as behaving more like an exalted one, though this is debated.

faq.q: which classical texts describe neech bhanga?
faq.a: phaladeepika by mantreswara gives clear rules, and brihat parashara hora shastra and later works discuss it. details vary slightly between texts.
